prompt: is the sentence this sentence is false true or false
reply:
Neither, and that is the whole point. If it is true, then what it claims holds, so it is false; if it is false, then it is telling the truth. Logicians call this the liar paradox. One common way out is to say the sentence gets no truth value at all — it points at itself in a way that breaks the rules truth normally needs. 🌀
